title: Working for Nat Shilkret on radio
summary: Shilkret was more of a musician, never cut him down, and the Saturday evening show had good sidemen but lasted one season.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: But this was the -- now, with Shilkret Shoret it was a little different. Shoret was more of a musician, and he was a little bit more of that style of the '20s. That's when he came up also.

And besides, he recorded so many bands that he had a great appreciation of what each band was like, and he was never like King down there. He never -- he always tried to help. If he could put in a little part, put a celeste part in, which he did for us one time, he would do things like that, never cut you down.

So I worked for him for three years after the Whiteman, after I got out of the Whiteman bands and he was excellent. We had a little style, and there was a little style to the band. We had a fine band, you know. Then we had both Dorseys and Artie Shaw. And guys like that we had in the band.
But I think the show come on about Saturday evening when it was -- what do they call that -- that's --
Yeah, but that is not prime time. That's in the -- that's the worst time you can get in radio, is Saturday evening.
Because people are all going out.
That's right. But we used to sound pretty good. We used to have mostly musicians would listen, but the show lasted, I think, one season, and then it -- they changed it, too, changed it around.
